knowledge:
- key_parameters: event_indicator=The column name in experiment_info representing the censoring indicator (1 for observed, 0 for censored), which is associated with the first element in cols_fixed ;; mi_reps=The number of multiple imputation repetitions to perform, where more imputations are needed for high censoring rates or high statistical power ;; imputation_method=The method used to impute censored values, such as "cc" (complete case), "rs" (risk set), "km" (Kaplan-Meier), or "mrl" (mean residual life) ;; BPPARAM=A BiocParallelParam object (e.g., MulticoreParam) used to parallelize the multiple imputation and testing steps
- alternatives: testDA_GLMM or testDA_edgeR from diffcyt (preferred when covariates are fully observed without censoring) ;; Complete case analysis / listwise deletion (simple but reduces statistical power and introduces bias under high or non-random censoring) ;; Cox proportional hazard models (standard survival analysis, but only applicable when the censored variable is the response rather than a covariate)
- when_to_use: Use when performing differential abundance analysis of cell populations in high-dimensional cytometry data where a key covariate of interest (e.g., patient survival time or time-to-event) is right-censored.
- pitfalls: If the largest value in the dataset is censored, the survival function does not reach 0, leaving some replacements undefined in Kaplan-Meier imputation; this requires specifying tail approximation methods (e.g., km_exp, km_wei, km_os) ;; Using too few imputation repetitions (mi_reps) when the censoring rate is high, which can lead to unstable estimates and reduced statistical power.

workflows.name: censored_da_step_by_step
workflows.intent: Perform differential abundance analysis with a censored covariate step-by-step using pre-calculated cluster counts.
input: d_counts (SummarizedExperiment containing cluster cell counts per sample)
experiment_info (data.frame containing sample IDs, observed covariate values, and event indicators)
workflows.stages: 1. Set up metadata and design formula using createFormula with an event indicator ;; 2. Define the contrast matrix ;; 3. Run differential testing using testDA_censoredGLMM with multiple imputation ;; 4. Extract top results using topTable
workflows.code:
da_formula <- createFormula(experiment_info = experiment_info,
                            cols_fixed = "X_obs",
                            cols_random = "sample_id",
                            event_indicator = "Event_ind")
# also create contrast matrix for testing
contrast <- matrix(c(0,1))

# test with 50 repetitions with method risk set imputation (rs)
da_out <- testDA_censoredGLMM(d_counts = d_counts,
                              formula = da_formula,
                              contrast = contrast,
                              mi_reps = 30,
                              imputation_method = "km",
                              verbose = TRUE,
                              BPPARAM=BiocParallel::MulticoreParam(workers = 1))

topTable(da_out)

workflows.name: censored_da_wrapper
workflows.intent: Perform the complete differential abundance analysis workflow (clustering and testing) from raw expression data using the censcyt wrapper.
input: d_input (list of matrices containing marker expression data per sample)
experiment_info (data.frame containing sample IDs, observed covariate values, and event indicators)
marker_info (data.frame containing channel names, marker names, and marker classes)
workflows.stages: 1. Set up metadata and design formula using createFormula with an event indicator ;; 2. Define the contrast matrix ;; 3. Run the all-in-one wrapper function censcyt to cluster cells and perform differential testing ;; 4. Extract top results using topTable and plot results using plotHeatmap
workflows.code:
da_formula <- createFormula(experiment_info = experiment_info,
                            cols_fixed = "X_obs",
                            cols_random = "sample_id",
                            event_indicator = "Event_ind")
# also create contrast matrix for testing
contrast <- matrix(c(0,1))

# Run wrapper function
out_DA <- censcyt(d_input, 
                  experiment_info, 
                  marker_info,
                  formula = da_formula, 
                  contrast = contrast,
                  meta_clustering = TRUE, 
                  meta_k = 10,
                  seed_clustering = 123, 
                  verbose = FALSE, 
                  mi_reps = 10,
                  imputation_method = "km",
                  BPPARAM=BiocParallel::MulticoreParam(workers = 1))

# Display results for top DA clusters
topTable(out_DA, format_vals = TRUE)

# Plot heatmap for DA tests
plotHeatmap(out_DA, 
            analysis_type = "DA", 
            sample_order = order(X_true))
